ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004, as amended. Every beneficial owner and signatory must be screened against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List and the Financial Action Task Force high-risk and other monitored jurisdictions list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must receive enhanced due diligence, including identification of source of wealth, source of funds and high-level approval by senior management. Additional domestic screening is performed through the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CRF) and the CSSF enforcement reporting channels. Continuous near-real-time sanctions and adverse media screening must be deployed for the life of the entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), official online portal at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in any language using the Latin alphabet. If a trade name is rendered in non-Latin script, a validated Latin-character transliteration must be filed as the registered formal name. The legal form suffix 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in the name. A name that is identical, misleading or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in Luxembourg is inadmissible.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the RCS/LBR, the applicant may file, within 15 days of the electronic rejection notice, a written administrative reconsideration through the LBR portal together with a revised proposed name and a legal memorandum explaining non-confusion and compliance with the mandatory corporate form suffix. If the administrative refusal is confirmed, the applicant may bring judicial review proceedings before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) within 30 days of the confirmation notice, with service through a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour. Such judicial appeal must be brought by formal petition and is subject to normal court filing fees and attorney costs. There is no additional official name-reservation extension, but a new identical name reservation may be filed after the expiry of the initial validity period if no conflicting application has been registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Commercial domiciliation through a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent is permissible for a SARL and will satisfy the formal registered-office requirement for purposes of RCS registration. However, for VAT and direct tax residence, the law requires a genuine seat of management in Luxembourg. For a TikTok Shop social-commerce retail entity operating through cross-border digital channels, a stand-alone virtual office without any administrative infrastructure, local personnel or decision-making heft cannot establish fiscal residence or adequate economic substance under Luxembourg anti-abuse jurisprudence and OECD BEPS standards. A domiciliation arrangement with a regulated agent plus a local compliance officer, a bank relationship in Luxembourg, local books and a real administrative mailbox is the accepted minimum substance package for this low-risk industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection by the RCS or Luxembourg tax authorities within the first year of registration; the likelihood increases to approximately 25% during the first 24 months if the company claims treaty benefits, applies for Luxembourg VAT and has a high volume of e-commerce transactions. For pure domiciliary companies with no local employees and no tax substance, inspection risk is assessed at 30% over the first three years.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (SARL regime), as modernized by the Law of 10 August 2016; access to the retail profession governed by the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on the establishment of commercial, artisanal, industrial and certain liberal activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), maintained under the authority of the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg), electronic portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif / statuts) executed before a Luxembourg civil-law notary, filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed at incorporation; at least 25% of each cash quota must be paid up (aggregate minimum EUR 3,000) and deposited into a blocked escrow account ('compte bloqué') opened in the name of the company in formation with a Luxembourg credit institution; funds are released only upon RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's (réviseur d'entreprises) valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned subscribers hereby adopt the Articles of Association of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) as contained in the notarial deed executed before the undersigned Luxembourg notary; that each subscriber irrevocably subscribes for the number of shares set opposite his name and pays the statutory minimum paid-up portion into the blocked escrow account held with a Luxembourg credit institution for the benefit of the company in formation; that the registered office of the company is fixed at the address of the company's central administration in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; and that [Name] is hereby appointed as Manager (Gérant), with full powers to file the deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers, arrange RESA publication, and open ordinary bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online portal (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name check and reservation request via the LBR portal. The proposed corporate name must comply with Luxembourg naming rules, be neither identical nor confusingly similar to existing RCS registrations, and include or complement the legal form indicator 'SARL'. Obtain the preliminary name clearance certificate before notarization.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to 3 alternatives)
Passport or EU national ID of each subscriber
Concise corporate purpose clause summary
Power of attorney of the filing agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected by the registrar, re-file with amended alternatives; a formal refusal may be appealed to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) selected by the subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the French-language notarial deed (acte constitutif) containing the SARL's name, registered office in Luxembourg, detailed corporate purpose covering retail sale via online and social-media platforms, share capital, distribution of quotas, management powers of the gérant, and duration (typically unlimited). All subscribers must appear before the notary or be validly represented by a power of attorney; the deed is read, approved and signed.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association prepared by the notary
Valid identity documents of all subscribers
Bank certificate evidencing opening of the blocked escrow account and deposit of the paid-up portion
Share subscription list signed by each subscriber
Certificate of name reservation from the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary identifies legal defects, amend the draft and re-execute; minimum capital and subscription formalities are mandatory and cannot be waived — rectify capital allocation, subscriber eligibility or corporate purpose wording prior to execution to avoid nullity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked escrow account and payment of minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) authorized by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account ('compte bloqué') in the name of the company in formation with a Luxembourg bank. For a SARL, deposit at least EUR 3,000 (25% of the EUR 12,000 minimum capital) from the subscribers' accounts. Obtain the bank's attestation of blockage confirming the deposit, the account holder and the beneficial owners; funds remain frozen until presentation of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Passport or ID of subscribers and proposed manager
AML/KYC forms, beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds evidence
Bank account opening questionnaire and risk profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues enhanced due-diligence queries, provide corroborating source-of-wealth documentation or an independent audit trail of funds; alternatively, increase the paid-up amount or effect an in-kind contribution supported by a réviseur d'entreprises report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the RCS and publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), District Court of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed and supporting exhibits electronically via the LBR portal within one month of notarization. The RCS verifies the legality of the deed and the capacity of the manager, issues the RCS registration number and publishes the incorporation in the RESA electronic compendium, conferring legal personality from the date of filing.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation
Bank attestation evidencing paid-up capital blockage
Manager's written consent to appointment
Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) of the manager
Proof of address of the registered office (lease or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a corrective query ('sursis à l'inscription'), cure the defect by submitting supplementary documents, amending the deed or replacing the manager; a refusal may be appealed before the District Court of Luxembourg within the legal delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration business establishment permit and administrative registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Middle Classes (Direction générale des Classes moyennes); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); competent commune
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) required under the Law of 2 September 2011 for retail trading activity, register for VAT with the AEDT (mandatory above EUR 35,000 annual turnover; voluntary registration allowed for social-commerce operations), enroll the company and manager with the CCSS for social security, and register the commercial premises with the commune for local business tax (impôt commercial communal).
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Business establishment permit application form
Identity documents, CV and management-capacity evidence of the manager
Certificate of non-criminal record (bulletin n°3)
Commercial lease or deed proving right to use the premises
VAT registration form (formulaire n°100/105)
CCSS employer and manager registration forms
Commune business tax registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Classes moyennes queries the manager's professional or managerial qualifications, supplement the file with formal training certificates or appoint a qualified manager; if VAT registration is delayed, request retroactive effect from the commencement of activity; administrative refusals may be appealed to the Minister of the Economy within 3 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Middle Classes (Direction générale des Classes moyennes)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the artisanal, commercial, industrial and liberal professions; no sector-specific license is required for social-commerce retail via the TikTok Shop model, but the establishment permit remains mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 – Registration / declaration only; a full EIA Report is not required for office and low-impact retail warehousing of packaged goods below the screening thresholds of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment. A waste declaration (déclaration de déchets) and a municipal wastewater discharge registration may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 May 1994 on non-domestic wastewater discharge (BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L) and the applicable municipal sewer ordinance; packaging waste take-back and recovery obligations under the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; WEEE and battery take-back obligations for returned e-commerce electrical goods; no significant VOC or combustion emission sources for pure warehousing/retail activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) covering evacuation routes, fire-extinguishing equipment and alarm systems; structural load and stability inspection of storage racks and mezzanines; electrical installation conformity certificate from an approved inspector; workplace safety and occupational health clearance (visite) by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including ergonomic and manual-handling risk assessment for order-picking staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (business registration), eTVA VAT filing desk, and guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SARL with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RBCS/LBR) through MyGuichet.lu and obtain the national 13-digit identification number (matricule). 2) File VAT registration Form 640 with the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits). 3) Non-resident entities making taxable supplies in Luxembourg without a domestic establishment must register for VAT through the AEDT (non-resident VAT registration) and, if established outside the EU/EEA without a fixed establishment, appoint an approved VAT representative in Luxembourg (Article 65 of the Luxembourg VAT Law). 4) Register any beneficial owner in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within one month of incorporation. 5) Submit supporting documents electronically: articles of association, proof of registered address, lease or service agreement, financial standing documents and powers of attorney; VAT ID is effective from the date the taxable activity commences or from the date of first taxable transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Luxembourg-resident SARL is a separate taxable person subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IRC), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune, IF). Territorial scope: resident entities are taxed on worldwide income with unilateral and treaty-based relief; qualified dividends and capital gains benefit from the participation exemption (10% or EUR 1.2 million participation thresholds; 12-month holding requirement). The SARL's shareholders are additionally taxable on distributed dividends.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box classification regime; tax status follows legal form (SARL = corporation). Available statutory elections: (i) VAT group option (assujetti unique, Article 61 VAT Law) allowing a single VAT registration for financially integrated resident entities; (ii) corporate income tax fiscal unity (intégration fiscale, Article 164bis LIR) for resident companies directly or indirectly holding 95% of a Luxembourg subsidiary; (iii) registration under the Union OSS or Import OSS schemes for cross-border distance sales and low-value consignments; (iv) binding advance tax ruling requests (Article 29a General Tax Law). Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD 1 and 2 are fully transposed (Article 168quater LIR; Articles 61-61c of the tax adaptation law); no elective hybrid-mismatch carve-out is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual VAT-exclusive Luxembourg turnover; small-business exemption threshold under Article 57 VAT Law as of 1 January 2025; voluntary registration permitted below the threshold). For EU distance sales of goods covered by the One Stop Shop regime, the EU-wide annual distance-sales threshold is EUR 10,000; non-established non-EU suppliers are registrable regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based transaction clearance applies to Luxembourg VAT. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory through the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 network and the national bill.lu e-invoicing platform; B2B and B2C invoicing remains voluntary (PDF, EDI or equivalent accepted), subject to recipient consent, authenticity and integrity control, and retention rights. A future mandatory structured e-invoicing (EN 16931) regime for cross-border B2B transactions is expected under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) directive, effective no earlier than 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) applies to (i) goods physically exported outside the European Union and evidenced by a customs export declaration, and (ii) services directly connected with such exports (transport, freight-handling, ancillary services) under Articles 70-74 of the Luxembourg VAT Law. For cross-border TikTok Shop retail consignments, 0% treatment requires proof of physical dispatch from Luxembourg, transport out of the EU, and the exporter's status as legal owner of the goods; consignments of intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 sold through an Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) scheme are VAT-relieved at the point of import. Intra-EU distance sales are subject to the Union OSS regime at the destination country's VAT rate. The 180-day export-proceeds benchmark serves as the audit-standard documentation window for the export file; Luxembourg VAT law does not separately impose a civil FX repatriation deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EAD/DRN) issued through the Luxembourg PLDA/ECS customs system, including MRN
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR international transport consignment note evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial invoice and packing list matching TikTok Shop order data
IOSS VAT identification number and IOSS sales list (for consignments with intrinsic value ≤ EUR 150)
Inward remittance evidence of export proceeds (SWIFT MT103, banking statement, or Wise B2B payout confirmation)
TikTok Shop marketplace payout report / platform sales certificate reconciled to the export documents
Customs broker representation authorization or indirect representation mandate, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or improperly substantiated export zero-rating claims trigger retrospective VAT reassessment at the standard 17% rate, with the limitation period extended from 5 to 10 years in cases of fraud, plus monthly default interest of 0.8% on unpaid VAT and clawback of all input VAT previously recovered in reliance on the invalid zero-rating. Administrative fines apply for documentation failures, and criminal prosecution under Article 93 of the VAT Law and the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) may result in fines up to EUR 250,000 (or double the evaded tax) and imprisonment of up to 5 years, with additional publication sanctions and professional disqualification of responsible managers. LuxLeaks-style whistleblower and administrative cooperation channels further increase audit scrutiny for cross-border marketplace sellers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting in concert with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and financial stability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible under EU free movement of capital and payments (TFEU Articles 63-66). Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, no prior authorisation for cross-border payments, and no restriction on repatriation of capital, dividends, interest, or profits. An SARL may freely convert EUR to any currency for business purposes. Dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at 15% (as reduced by double tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive), but there is no currency convertibility or central-bank approval hurdle. Injected share capital may be returned to shareholders without material FX restrictions, subject to notarial/registry and corporate law compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg has no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender and no mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts. Exporters may retain all EUR or foreign-currency proceeds and are not required to transfer them to the BCL or any state entity. Documentary retention obligations under customs, VAT, and AML regulations remain the primary compliance requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex are legally viable for cross-border payment settlement and operating expenditures under the EEA passport framework. They are not licensed as full credit institutions and therefore may not serve as the principal treasury or capital-escrow bank for a Luxembourg SARL. Their utility is strongest for fast TikTok Shop merchant payouts, FX conversions, and low-value cross-border supplier disbursements. Legal constraints include the absence of Luxembourg Credit Institution status, reduced depositor protection coverage, and bank-specific KYC onboarding limitations on high-volume e-commerce flows. A hybrid model — primary institutional bank account plus an EMI sub-ledger for high-speed clearing — is prudent and widely accepted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML laws require reliable customer due diligence under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation No 12-02. A director/manager (gérant) need not appear physically at every bank if the bank adopts certified video identification and secure e-signature protocols; however, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks prefer a physical opening session or an in-person visit by an authorised local representative to complete the beneficial-ownership waterfall and politically-exposed-person (PEP) checks. Remote account opening is permissible in principle, but each bank's internal risk policy may require at least one physical attendance or notarised certified passport copies and apostilled corporate documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume TikTok Shop payout flows with no VAT-compliant invoice trail and no documented underlying merchant agreements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the duly signed TikTok Shop seller agreement and target-commission annex, monthly settlement statements from the platform covering gross sales, fees, and net payouts, a structured revenue ledgers exported to an accounting file, Luxembourg VAT returns (form 1027) with intra-Community and export VAT position, and transaction-level pay-in/payout reconciliation logs matched to purchase orders and delivery proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from non-EU shareholders with unclear source of wealth or missing tax residence documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarised articles of association and share subscription documents, recent bank statements from the shareholders' financial institutions showing the source and trail of funds, certificates of incorporation and tax residence certificates from the shareholder jurisdictions, and a clear group ownership chart evidencing no sanctions, no significant-money-laundering-risk, and no unresolved tax controversies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of Luxembourg economic substance resulting in unjustified pass-through or cross-border transaction flagging.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a Luxembourg office lease or serviced-office agreement, local payroll and management appointment records, board/manager meeting minutes held in Luxembourg, a functional and operational risk assessment confirming that treasury, invoicing, and TikTok Shop control activities are performed in Luxembourg, and a transfer-pricing memorandum documenting arm's-length intra-group fees and markups.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement to merchants in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions via digital wallet infrastructures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide sub-merchant KYC files with passport and residence proof, sanctions-screening results using an automated screening tool, contractual warranties on underlying digital goods/services sales, a tax opinion on non-EU VAT/GST handling, and a legal analysis confirming that the TikTok Shop activity does not constitute an unlicensed electronic-money or payment-service operation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should be routed through SWIFT MT103 messages using purpose code CAPT (Capital Injection to a Subsidiary) or GFC (Funding of a Branch/Subsidiary). The remitter must include the Luxembourg SARL's full corporate name, commercial registry number, and the specific bank account IBAN. The bank may require the initial capital confirmation from the Luxembourg Trade Register (LBR) or a notary's certificate for the souscription and libération of shares. The European wire-transfer regulation (EU) No 2023/1113 and AML provisions impose mandatory originator/beneficiary information. No BCL approval or pre-approval for FX conversion is required; any EUR/USD or EUR/CNY conversion may be completed at the receiving bank's applicable spot rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements to suppliers and logistics providers are cleared through SWIFT MT103 or SEPA instant/regular credit transfers for EU counterparties. For high-value inventory or supply-chain purchases, commercial letters of credit (L/C) issued by the Luxembourg bank and confirmed through a correspondent bank provide the preferred clearing rail. Each disbursement must be supported by an invoice, packing list, transport document (B/L or airway bill), and, when applicable, proof of intra-Community VAT-exempt supply or export VAT zero-rating. The bank will normally apply market-standard FX margins and may require a standing execution order for recurring TikTok Shop inventory payments in CNY or USD.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards – physically settled EUR/USD and EUR/CNY forwards with maturities up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA or local FX master agreement with a licensed Luxembourg bank.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permitted for currencies with delivery restrictions (e.g., CNY, KRW, INR) through the Luxembourg bank's international branch, with settlement in EUR or USD on fix dates referencing the offshore currency rate.
FX Swaps / Rollovers – simultaneous spot and forward transactions to manage interim liquidity mismatches between TikTok Shop payout timing and supplier payment deadlines.
FX Options – vanilla call and put options on EUR pairs providing asymmetric hedge protection, subject to bank OTC derivative eligibility and mandatory margining rules under EMIR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (bilan, compte de profits et pertes, annexe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; shareholder approval must be given within six months after fiscal year-end (for a 31 December year-end, approval by 30 June and RCS filing by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 10,000 and default interest; publication delays subject to daily penalties; persistent non-filing may lead to administrative dissolution or judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation (confirmation of beneficial ownership register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following each annual registration anniversary; any share-transfer update to the beneficial owner register within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 and criminal penalties for intentional non-disclosure; managers may face imprisonment in serious cases; the annual fee remains enforceable after the deadline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., FY ending 31 December 2024: due 31 December 2025); an e-file extension may defer subject to ACD approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due (minimum EUR 250), default interest, administrative fines, and possible ex officio tax assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (same tax deadline as corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and default interest as for corporate income tax; net wealth tax minimum assessment may be imposed even if no return is filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (déclaration de TVA) and annual recapitulative statement if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT return due by the 30th of the following month; annual recapitulative statement (if required) due 31 May of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing or late-payment surcharge up to 10% of tax due, default interest, and administrative penalties enforced by AEDT

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a réviseur d'entreprises agréé when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: total balance-sheet assets above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average annual employees above 50 full-time equivalents. Audit also applies to companies forming part of a consolidated group, public companies, and financial holding undertakings (SOPARFI) meeting regulatory asset thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg Commercial Code, plan comptable applicable) for the statutory annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is mandatory for entities with securities listed on an EU regulated market and may be voluntarily applied by others.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE confirmation must be filed once per calendar year, within one month after the anniversary of the company's RBE registration. Confirmation is made electronically through the LBR portal (via the registered agent when applicable). Any change in beneficial ownership resulting from a share transfer must be filed separately within one month of the transfer; the annual confirmation does not replace the transfer-triggered update and must reflect the entire current shareholding structure. If no change occurred, the confirmation simply certifies the existing register.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined, comprising 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on the corporate income tax (1.19% aggregate), and Luxembourg City municipal business tax of 6.75%; the municipal business tax rate varies by commune between approximately 6.75% and 10.10%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying participation exemption (100% exemption for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% or EUR 6 million held for at least 12 months); IP Box regime granting an 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income, producing an effective tax rate of approximately 4.99%; Notional Interest Deduction on qualifying new equity; R&D tax credit up to 25% of eligible expenditure (subject to statutory ceilings); no general statutory tax holiday or preferential territorial regime for social commerce or TikTok Shop retail activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite — no statutory expiry under Article 110 LIR, provided the company continues the same business activity and does not fall within anti-loss-buying rules applicable upon a change of control or business scope.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 105 (Formulaire 105) — Déclaration de l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, filed through MyGuichet.lu (Luxembourg’s official public administration electronic filing portal) and the ACD electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return for a fiscal year must be filed electronically no later than 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; extensions are discretionary and subject to ACD approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, RCS registration number, Luxembourg matricule (tax identification number), fiscal year dates, and designated tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders or a foreign head office must identify a Luxembourg fiscal representative or filing agent and declare all Luxembourg-source income attributable to the SARL, including TikTok Shop sales and influencer commission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit and loss statement prepared under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS, including turnover, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and net taxable result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the financial statements with bank settlement payloads from TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B; disclosing all revenue streams is mandatory for SARL entities economically active in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 — Profit allocation and permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule allocating taxable income to Luxembourg, including direct sales, warehousing, logistics, advertising services, and any permanent establishment factors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If TikTok Shop retail operations are conducted through a Luxembourg warehouse or fulfillment centre, the SARL must disclose whether a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists and allocate profit accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to accounting result for non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, participation exemption, IP Box deduction, notional interest deduction, loss carryforward, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief claims must be supported by a valid certificate of tax residence from the foreign parent jurisdiction; the SARL must demonstrate beneficial ownership and economic substance for relief to apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Declarations for municipal business tax and net wealth tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of municipal business tax base and Luxembourg net wealth tax position, including taxable net equity and any deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owed SARLs must ensure the municipal business tax is reported at the correct communal rate and that net wealth tax returns are consistent with the corporate income tax filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may result in ex officio assessment by the ACD, mandatory late payment interest of 0.8% per month, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, and, in cases of intentional false declarations, criminal tax fraud penalties of up to EUR 500,000 plus imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on dividends distributed by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident shareholders, unless a Domestic Law exemption or Double Tax Treaty provides a lower rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief is obtained either at source through the paying entity or by filing a refund application with the Luxembourg tax authorities. The recipient must submit a current Luxembourg Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) of the state of residence, evidence of beneficial ownership, confirmation of shareholding duration, and, where applicable, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive holding requirements (at least 10% for 12 uninterrupted months) to obtain the 0% directive exemption or treaty-reduced rate, generally 5% or 15% depending on the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on arm's-length interest or royalty payments made by a SARL to non-resident corporate beneficiaries. Under various Luxembourg DTAs, outbound interest and royalties generally remain at 0% or are reduced to no more than 10% where source-State taxing rights exist.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No single universal transaction threshold is published in the Luxembourg Income Tax Law. The ACD expects a full OECD-aligned Transfer Pricing Master File and Local File for Luxembourg entities forming part of a multinational group with global consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or greater (CoCR threshold). Smaller groups should maintain contemporaneous local TP documentation when cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 500,000 in aggregate or when the Luxembourg entity's annual turnover surpasses EUR 10,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is not an Economic Substance Regulations jurisdiction, but the ACD applies the OECD-style economic substance and substance-over-form doctrine through the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR), ATAD anti-hybrid legislation, Circular LIR 14/6, and Pillar Two global minimum tax rules. A SARL relying on treaty benefits or holding-company exemptions must demonstrate local decision-making, personnel, premises, and real economic activity commensurate with its digital retail operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting or omitting TikTok Shop sales revenue, using fictitious supplier invoices, artificially shifting profit to affiliated platforms through overpriced marketing or logistics fees, or maintaining dual undisclosed bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax assessment, 0.8% monthly late-payment interest, administrative fines up to EUR 500,000, confiscation of the improperly shifted profit, and criminal fines of up to EUR 500,000 on conviction for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts when they have signed false returns, abusively drained corporate assets, or knowingly permitted fictitious invoicing; criminal conviction may carry imprisonment of up to five years, travel bans, and civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a letterbox SARL with no local employees, no physical office, no board minutes, no commercial activity in Luxembourg, and using the entity merely to route TikTok Shop commissions or obtain tax-treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of treaty benefits, denial of participation exemption, retroactive reclassification of income under GAAR, application of Pillar Two substance rules, net wealth tax recalculations, and supplementary tax assessments with penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto directors and shadow managers may be treated as taxable persons or managers of the sham entity, incurring personal income tax exposure, civil liability for the tax shortfall, and potential criminal sanction for fraudulent use of a corporate vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register and maintain accurate ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) information in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), laundering illicit TikTok Shop proceeds through crypto conversion, or concealing the identity of the actual controlling shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the RBE framework up to EUR 250,000 and criminal fines for money laundering of up to EUR 1,250,000, together with asset freezes and closure of the SARL's bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be criminally prosecuted for money laundering, incurring imprisonment, restrictive travel measures, personal asset forfeiture, and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating TikTok Shop retail without proper Luxembourg VAT registration, failing to charge the correct Luxembourg VAT rates, using another marketplace's VAT liability to mask local sales, or abusing the IOSS import scheme for goods delivered into Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessments, penalty interest, fines of up to EUR 250,000, and potential suspension of the marketplace account where the Luxembourg tax authorities issue a joint liability claim against the platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally directed the false VAT position may be jointly liable for the unpaid VAT, may be subject to travel bans during criminal proceedings, and may face imprisonment in aggravated fraud cases.
